integrity.description: The agent used the TiddlyWiki web interface to create tiddlers rather than manipulating the underlying file system via terminal.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the browser with the TiddlyWiki 'plus' button clicked, tiddler edit fields being filled, and 'save' buttons being pressed.

integrity.description: The agent authored realistic sentences for the ADR bodies rather than using placeholder text like 'lorem ipsum'.
integrity.visual_evidence: The text under !! Context, !! Decision, and !! Consequences contains meaningful words related to the ADR title (e.g., mentioning 'database' for ADR-001).

integrity.description: The ADR Index uses functional TiddlyWiki widgets rather than a hardcoded static list of links.
integrity.visual_evidence: The edit mode of the 'ADR Index' tiddler shows the <$list> syntax instead of just a bulleted list of manual links.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The required statuses are: ADR-001 (Accepted), ADR-002 (Accepted), ADR-003 (Deprecated), ADR-004 (Proposed), and ADR-005 (Accepted). ADR-003 must link to ADR-005 as its successor, and ADR-005 must link back to ADR-003 as the tiddler it supersedes. The ADR Index must use the specific filter syntax [tag[ADR]adr-status[Value]] within a list widget.
